label: weak conjunction of token identities (first token y/m/1, input 1/b/0/3/g after f/3/c/g) in the original phase
explanation: Sparse, low-magnitude feature (max 0.25, about 0.05% of steps). 96% of activation mass is in the original phase at t>=2, never at t=0-1, and it is nearly silent in the copy phase. It peaks on the last original step (to_go=0) and at the <DEL> step it fires weakly. Firing looks like an additive mix of weak token-identity cues: the first token is y (lift 15.7x, 54% of mass), m or 1; the input is 1/b/0/3/g; the previous token is f/3/c/g; the token two back is g. No single cue or small conjunction is anywhere near sufficient. first_tok==y alone has 3% precision, and the best conjunction reaches F1 0.17 on dev (precision 0.14, recall 0.21). I did not establish what drives magnitude beyond higher rates at late original positions and in longer sequences.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=y (+5.59), orig0=m (+4.14), orig0=1 (+3.79), in_tok=1 (+3.52), prev_tok=f (+3.19), phase=2 & out_tok=y (+3.05). Lower it: prev2_tok=- (-4.73), prev2_tok=1 (-3.40), prev3_tok=m (-3.34), prev2_tok=y (-3.29).
